1. The implementation MUST use the LensKit library (lenskit package) for all data handling, model training, and evaluation — not OmniRec, RecBole, or other frameworks.

2. Load three datasets: MovieLens 100K (via lenskit.data.load_movielens), Amazon Video Games 2014 (via lenskit.data.load_amazon_ratings), and Last.FM Hetrec 2011 (load from raw CSV using lenskit.data.from_interactions_df or standard pandas + DatasetBuilder).

3. Preprocess ALL three datasets with 5-core filtering (iteratively remove users and items with fewer than 5 interactions until convergence). For MovieLens 100K and Amazon Video Games, additionally convert explicit ratings to implicit feedback by keeping only interactions with rating > 3. Hetrec Last.FM (already implicit) must NOT receive rating thresholding.

4. Use user-based holdout splitting: for each dataset, generate 5 train-test splits using lenskit.splitting.sample_users or crossfold_users with SampleFrac(0.2) (80/20 user-based split). Each split must be controlled by a distinct random seed (via the rng parameter).

5. Train exactly three recommendation algorithms on each split: (a) ImplicitMFScorer (ALS for implicit feedback), (b) ItemKNNScorer configured for implicit feedback (feedback='implicit'), and (c) PopScorer (popularity baseline). Use default hyperparameters for all algorithms.

6. Evaluate all trained models using LensKit's top-N ranking metrics: Precision@k and NDCG@k for k=1, 5, and 10. Use RunAnalysis with Precision and NDCG metrics to compute per-user scores, then aggregate.
7. The experiment must produce results for all combinations: 3 datasets × 3 algorithms × 5 random seeds = 45 evaluation result sets, each reporting Precision@1,5,10 and NDCG@1,5,10.

8. Conduct a statistical analysis quantifying variance across the 5 random seeds per (dataset, algorithm) pair: report mean and standard deviation of each metric across seeds to measure the impact of data split randomness on accuracy.
